Hey Tom / Aisha,

Great questions — happy to clarify.

Short answers:
- Yes: Redwood supports both long-lived API keys and service accounts backed by the OAuth2 client_credentials flow using signed JWT assertions. We validate JWKS where applicable.
- Token TTLs: default access token TTL is 1 hour for service-account tokens; refresh/renew via new JWT assertion. For API keys we recommend rotating monthly, but best practice is to use service accounts for prod.
- Managed rotation: For hosted (Redwood Cloud) we offer a managed key rotation option for API keys and short-lived tokens. For Dedicated/Private we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) or HSM for key material; we can sign JWTs using KMS-backed keys.
- Audit logs: Redwood Console exposes token-level audit logs (token id, principal, route/model accessed, timestamp, and request id). These can be streamed to your logging endpoint (S3/CloudWatch/GCS).

Sample client_credentials curl (signed JWT assertion) — Node/Python SDKs handle signing for you; we include this for transparency:

# create JWT assertion (pseudo)
{
  "iss": "paymentsco-service-account@paymentsco.com",
  "sub": "paymentsco-service-account@paymentsco.com",
  "aud": "https://auth.redwood.ai/token",
  "exp": <now + 300>,
  "iat": <now>
}

curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer&assertion=<SIGNED_JWT>"

Response: {"access_token":"<short-lived-token>","expires_in":3600,"token_type":"Bearer"}

Attachments: redwood-service-account-sample.sh

Additional notes:
- SDKs will accept the short-lived token and automatically refresh using the client_credentials flow.
- For scoping, we recommend minting tokens with route claims (model:embedding, env:staging) to limit blast radius.
- I can share a minimal PoC repo and a short runbook for SRE to spin up a staging integration.

Link to docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/authentication/service-accounts
